review_items.rationale:
Reviewed fixed artifact b1dd572dd2d0465fbbc06af7dd312ac7 version 1 (plan and executed assurance_generated_test.go), its C_SINGLETON_READ_ELIGIBILITY version 1 basis, and execution 7f87025ec21040378846ee18bc957845 raw events and monitor correlations. The selected requirement is the derived local responsibility for communication-free singleton certification, supported by S_READ_SAFE_EXPECTATION (safe read quorum support) and S_SINGLETON_EXPECTATION (the sole voter is the leader). It does not assert that every ReadIndex returns, nor that ReadState emission completes a client read. S_TRACKER establishes cardinality only; the independent oracle additionally checks the invoking ID is the incoming voter and that no outgoing voters exist. This expectation is not derived solely from the fact that the implementation omits that check.

The selected entry is RawNode.ReadIndex on the same live instance that applied its committed removal. S_API supplies caller serialization; S_READ_API has no removal precondition; S_REMOVAL_OPTION explicitly controls removal step-down without stating that disabling it disables ReadOnlySafe. The driver keeps the removed object live as required by the fixed scope; external retirement policies are excluded, rather than presumed ineffective. Both nodes start with a consistent supplied index/term-1 snapshot and HardState. Actual campaigns elect node 1; Propose and actual append replies commit the old value and self-removal; the application worker activates the real committed configuration entry at index 4 on both nodes. Node 2 then campaigns using its installed singleton configuration and commits/applies a new value at index 6. These are one continuous execution per option, not stitched fragments. MemoryStorage processing precedes attached response delivery, application is index-ordered and calls ApplyConfChange only for returned committed entries. No state assignment creates removal, role retention, read response or voter identity. No crash or runtime snapshot is used. The small group is permitted; S_MEMBERSHIP_DOC recommends larger groups because of availability on failure, and this execution has no failed participant. The finite absence of ticks, with CheckQuorum disabled and explicit campaigns, does not omit a required safety guard for this chosen configuration.

Each request has independent identity (step_down, node, request_id). Unique contexts distinguish the removed-node read and current-singleton control; subtest identity separates the two histories. read_admitted is the declared prerequisite and precedes the actual ReadIndex call. The driver snapshots eligibility directly from active voter maps before invocation, records those maps, and copies that observed Boolean into the result summary; it is not an expected/precomputed failure. ReadState output is obtained from real Ready.ReadStates and independently filtered by emitting node and request context; result_count and read_index are raw derived observations. read_completed is emitted after unconditional pump quiescence, not contingent on receiving a result or on satisfying the property. The driver does not mutate configuration during a read interval. For the emitting case, raw read_state confirms the summary; for the nonemitting control, the finite summary reports false without turning that into a liveness claim.

The monitor checks returned implies self_sole_voter, rather than equality between availability and eligibility. In the witness (event 13 correlated to admission 11), step_down=false, node=1 and request_id=removed-after-write identify a real returned ReadState at index 4 with result_count=1, while voters=[2] and self_sole_voter=false. The branch correspondence follows actual StateLeader dispatch, singleton voter count, and S_SINGLETON_READ immediate response; there was no previous request with that context and the direct branch returns before any read heartbeat round. Thus the independently observed necessary qualification is false while the corresponding certification is present. The implementation/expectation discrepancy is the subject being checked, not a conflict among normative sources.

All four admitted operations correlate with four completion summaries and there are no parser errors or missing operations. Node 2 valid-singleton controls return index 6 with eligibility true. The step_down=true removed-node control reports returned=false, as permitted; it is a diagnostic outside the claim parameter StepDownOnRemoval=false and contributes no violating witness or broader positive conclusion. The main witness alone lies fully within the recorded claim scope. The controls support the observed role-protection distinction but are not exhaustive cause isolation. The raw successor-write history illustrates possible consequence but is not part of the oracle and does not establish a served stale application read. In particular the removed application index equals the returned read index, so the strict greater-than reading of S_READ_API is not demonstrated. No correspondence issue was found for this local certification proposition.

formation.explanation: A serialized RawNode caller or node.run admits Propose into raft.Step. Followers may forward; candidates or leaderless followers drop. A leader assigns term/index, appends unstable entries, queues a self acknowledgement and replicates MsgApp with predecessor identity. Followers validate the predecessor, refuse committed conflicts, truncate only uncommitted suffixes, and queue append responses. send separates these responses from immediately sendable messages. In async mode ordered durable append work releases responses; synchronous Ready/Advance splits remote and self delivery under caller persistence duties. The leader term-filters replies, requires sender progress, updates Match monotonically, computes the majority-supported index (both majorities for joint membership), and advances only if that index has the current term. Commit is propagated in appends; heartbeats cap commit at the recipient Match. Followers cap append commit at their matched request suffix. Ready exposes committed work with snapshot and application-size guards; async mode additionally requires local stabilization. Applied callbacks are distinct from Ready acceptance and client completion. Propose success promises no commitment.

context.explanation: Authority belongs to a raft instance in a term and installed voter configuration. Election ticks or Campaign require promotability and no unapplied committed configuration change. PreVote can probe the next term without changing current term/vote; real campaigning increments term and queues durable self-vote support. Vote recipients check previous vote/known leader and candidate last-entry freshness. Candidates tally only the response type matching their phase, using configured voter majorities. Winning real election resets progress and appends a current-term empty entry. Higher-term messages generally install follower state, with explicit pre-vote and lease exceptions; stale messages are normally ignored. CheckQuorum may remove leadership; transfer pauses proposals and waits for transferee catch-up. Membership activates through caller application of committed configuration entries, using simple/joint transitions and retained progress. Restart reconstructs saved term/vote/commit and membership but starts follower with no leader. Snapshot acceptance checks obsolescence, follower state and recipient membership before restoring history/configuration or fast-forwarding matching commit.

connection.explanation: Role reset discards vote tallies and remote Match, retains local history/commit, initializes self Match from that history and rebuilds readOnly acknowledgements. A new current-term entry plus quorum/current-term commitment reconnects retained history to new leadership. Configuration activation can reinterpret retained Match and call maybeCommit without a fresh reply. Old queued responses can survive emission, so consumers enforce term filtering; storage append completion additionally matches entry index/log term before trimming unstable memory. Snapshot completion from an older term remains processed, and application responses have term zero, reflecting committed state that outlives authority. Pending read requests awaiting first current-term commit survive reset separately from readOnly acknowledgement state: they are released only after a current-term commit and then enter the selected read confirmation mechanism. Safe reads correlate heartbeat acknowledgements by context and installed voters; returned ReadState is still subject to caller application progress. These mechanisms separate volatile support, established local decisions, durable state and externally served results.

items.rationale:
Reviewed the fixed plan and assurance_generated_test.go for artifact 30b99642cd6d4bb89f9e66b2d66afa77 version 1, its C_STALE_APPEND_COMPLETION version 1 basis, and raw execution e79e31386cd248c8bacd4ffbecbac979 plus parsed correlations. The requirement comes from S_COMPLETION_EXPECTATION, not from the observed guard: an old raft-term append completion must not truncate unstable entries. S_STABLE_EXPECTATION explains why entry identity alone is insufficient. RawNode is the actual selected entry and all calls are serialized. The prefix is an explicitly supplied consistent snapshot/HardState at index/term 1 with voters 1/2/3; the test does not claim to execute that prefix production. After construction, actual Campaign, Propose, Ready, MemoryStorage writes and Step execute the history without assigning protocol state or fabricating responses. The append worker processes each node work in Ready order, saves entries and nonempty HardState before releasing responses, and finitely holds only node 3 MsgStorageAppendResp. Those held messages are later consumed unchanged and in production order. Modeled storage completion means successful MemoryStorage calls in a noncrashing execution, not disk durability. Normal-entry no-op application and omission of ticks do not interfere with the selected synchronous completion consumer: there are no application-dependent configuration entries, elections are explicitly driven, and CheckQuorum is disabled.

Identity is (node, marker_id), assigned from held-list position at producer emission and retained by the same immutable pending sequence at consumption. It is independent of response term/index and unstable offset, so repeated marker tuples remain distinct. The origin event occurs after storage processing; the before event occurs immediately before the specific Step call and references origin.response_term as a predecessor constraint. The completed event follows Step return unconditionally. Raw terms and entry identity are emitted; stale is computed before Step as response.Term < raft.Term, independently of the offset comparison. All five marker identities have one origin, one admission and one completion. The monitor selected before as admission_alias and correlated events 9/11/13/15/17 to their respective origins and admissions, with no parsing errors or missing results.

For markers 0 and 1, response term 2 is below receiving term 3 and entry (3,2) still matches. Both comparisons observe unstable offset 3 before and after Step. The current-term marker 2 from a zero-entry append has the same entry identity and advances offset 3 to 4; marker 3 advances 4 to 5, and duplicate marker 4 leaves it 5. These latter operations are permitted controls, not required-success instances: event_implication applies the equality assertion only when stale is true. The independent expected relation is offset_after = before.unstable_offset, directly encoding no prefix truncation because stableTo removes prefix entries by advancing offset. No event interleaves within Step, and no snapshot is present to introduce an independent completion effect. The final pump observes applied=committed=4 and no held markers; final application is diagnostic, whereas synchronous Step completion is the required endpoint.

This supports the runner bounded holds measurement for the two stale completion instances and its complete per-operation correlation. The result answers local context-fence consumption in this history, not the broader causal hypothesis about ABA overwrites or consensus divergence. No correspondence issue was found within this fixed scope; that review judgment is not an overall proof.

Source protections and alternative branches considered: The implementation already has an explicit raft-term filter and an additional entry index/log-term guard; the execution is consistent with these protections, not evidence of a defect. Old-term snapshot completion is intentionally handled even when entry completion is rejected; all checked responses are snapshot-free. Fresh-term completion for an old entry term is permitted and observed, so treating entry term as the invalidating context would be wrong.

formation.explanation: A serialized RawNode caller or node.run admits Propose into raft.Step. Followers may forward; candidates or leaderless followers drop. A leader assigns term/index, appends unstable entries, queues a self acknowledgement and replicates MsgApp with predecessor identity. Followers validate the predecessor, refuse committed conflicts, truncate only uncommitted suffixes, and queue append responses. send separates these responses from immediately sendable messages. In async mode ordered durable append work releases responses; synchronous Ready/Advance splits remote and self delivery under caller persistence duties. The leader term-filters replies, requires sender progress, updates Match monotonically, computes the majority-supported index (both majorities for joint membership), and advances only if that index has the current term. Commit is propagated in appends; heartbeats cap commit at the recipient Match. Followers cap append commit at their matched request suffix. Ready exposes committed work with snapshot and application-size guards; async mode additionally requires local stabilization. Applied callbacks are distinct from Ready acceptance and client completion. Propose success promises no commitment.

context.explanation: Authority belongs to a raft instance in a term and installed voter configuration. Election ticks or Campaign require promotability and no unapplied committed configuration change. PreVote can probe the next term without changing current term/vote; real campaigning increments term and queues durable self-vote support. Vote recipients check previous vote/known leader and candidate last-entry freshness. Candidates tally only the response type matching their phase, using configured voter majorities. Winning real election resets progress and appends a current-term empty entry. Higher-term messages generally install follower state, with explicit pre-vote and lease exceptions; stale messages are normally ignored. CheckQuorum may remove leadership; transfer pauses proposals and waits for transferee catch-up. Membership activates through caller application of committed configuration entries, using simple/joint transitions and retained progress. Restart reconstructs saved term/vote/commit and membership but starts follower with no leader. Snapshot acceptance checks obsolescence, follower state and recipient membership before restoring history/configuration or fast-forwarding matching commit.

connection.explanation: Role reset discards vote tallies and remote Match, retains local history/commit, initializes self Match from that history and rebuilds readOnly acknowledgements. A new current-term entry plus quorum/current-term commitment reconnects retained history to new leadership. Configuration activation can reinterpret retained Match and call maybeCommit without a fresh reply. Old queued responses can survive emission, so consumers enforce term filtering; storage append completion additionally matches entry index/log term before trimming unstable memory. Snapshot completion from an older term remains processed, and application responses have term zero, reflecting committed state that outlives authority. Pending read requests awaiting first current-term commit survive reset separately from readOnly acknowledgement state: they are released only after a current-term commit and then enter the selected read confirmation mechanism. Safe reads correlate heartbeat acknowledgements by context and installed voters; returned ReadState is still subject to caller application progress. These mechanisms separate volatile support, established local decisions, durable state and externally served results.

It does not assert that every ReadIndex returns, nor that ReadState emission completes a client read. S_TRACKER establishes cardinality only; the independent oracle additionally checks the invoking ID is the incoming voter and that no outgoing voters exist. This expectation is not derived solely from the fact that the implementation omits that check.

The selected entry is RawNode.ReadIndex on the same live instance that applied its committed removal. S_API supplies caller serialization; S_READ_API has no removal precondition; S_REMOVAL_OPTION explicitly controls removal step-down without stating that disabling it disables ReadOnlySafe. The driver keeps the removed object live as required by the fixed scope; external retirement policies are excluded, rather than presumed ineffective. Both nodes start with a consistent supplied index/term-1 snapshot and HardState. Actual campaigns elect node 1; Propose and actual append replies commit the old value and self-removal; the application worker activates the real committed configuration entry at index 4 on both nodes. Node 2 then campaigns using its installed singleton configuration and commits/applies a new value at index 6. These are one continuous execution per option, not stitched fragments. MemoryStorage processing precedes attached response delivery, application is index-ordered and calls ApplyConfChange only for returned committed entries. No state assignment creates removal, role retention, read response or voter identity. No crash or runtime snapshot is used. The small group is permitted; S_MEMBERSHIP_DOC recommends larger groups because of availability on failure, and this execution has no failed participant. The finite absence of ticks, with CheckQuorum disabled and explicit campaigns, does not omit a required safety guard for this chosen configuration.

Each request has independent identity (step_down, node, request_id). Unique contexts distinguish the removed-node read and current-singleton control; subtest identity separates the two histories. read_admitted is the declared prerequisite and precedes the actual ReadIndex call. The driver snapshots eligibility directly from active voter maps before invocation, records those maps, and copies that observed Boolean into the result summary; it is not an expected/precomputed failure. ReadState output is obtained from real Ready.ReadStates and independently filtered by emitting node and request context; result_count and read_index are raw derived observations. read_completed is emitted after unconditional pump quiescence, not contingent on receiving a result or on satisfying the property. The driver does not mutate configuration during a read interval. For the emitting case, raw read_state confirms the summary; for the nonemitting control, the finite summary reports false without turning that into a liveness claim.
